independentSourceInventory.pixelObservation: One eye outline above the object, with a small eye-lens shape at the entrance and two ray continuations inside. A short opposite-side retinal interval is present. No photoreceptor detail or anatomical dimensions are given.
independentSourceInventory.candidateComparison: The horizontal candidate places the eye at the right, retains the entrance-lens outline, and carries the oblique ray to the opposite side of the horizontal reference.

independentSourceInventory.pixelObservation: The lower short interval is labelled h. Its endpoints bound the near-axial reference and oblique viewing ray. The reference goes through the eye and continues inside it; no grid, ticks, numerical lengths or point names appear.
independentSourceInventory.candidateComparison: Object-base and object-tip lie on one vertical h interval; object-base, eye-centre and retinal-axis share the horizontal baseline. The height is perpendicular to that baseline. No separate frame or extra calibrated axis is introduced.

independentSourceInventory.pixelObservation: An oblique line runs from one h endpoint toward the eye, with a direction mark toward the eye. The other endpoint supplies the axial direction. The oblique continuation lies on the opposite retinal side from the object endpoint.
independentSourceInventory.candidateComparison: The arrow points toward eye-centre. Object-tip, unaided-ray-mid and eye-centre are collinear; object-tip, eye-centre and retinal-tip are also collinear. The retinal interval is on the opposite side of the baseline from the object tip.

independentSourceInventory.pixelObservation: The phi mark denotes the wedge between the two object-endpoint directions at the eye. It is a symbolic viewing angle, not a graduated protractor or a stated exact angle.
independentSourceInventory.candidateComparison: The arc is centred on eye-centre. Its two endpoints have equal radius and lie on the object-tip and object-base directions respectively. The visible phi label identifies this wedge rather than an unrelated eye or dimension angle.

independentSourceInventory.pixelObservation: A d0 bracket extends from the object interval to the eye entrance/reference point. No 25 cm label is printed in the source figure itself; that convention comes from the associated text.
independentSourceInventory.candidateComparison: The candidate's horizontal d0 dimension projects from object-base to eye-centre and has the same span as that object-eye baseline. It does not measure the eyeball or extend to the retinal image.

science.finding: The unaided reference geometry supports phi approximately h/d0 for small angles in radians; h is the compared linear size and d0 is the axial object-eye distance. The figure supplies no exact-angle value and makes no relaxed-eye assertion.
